questions.subject: math
questions.question: In 4/4 time a melody begins with one quarter note before the first full bar. How many beats does that opening bar contain?
questions.explanation: The first bar holds only what is played before the first full measure: one beat.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: Where is the missing count of a pickup bar usually found?
options: In the last bar of the piece
questions.correct_answer: In the last bar of the piece
questions.explanation: The opening and closing bars together make one complete measure.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: A piece begins with an incomplete measure before the first full bar. What is this called?
questions.explanation: An incomplete opening measure is an anacrusis, also called a pickup bar.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: Another name for an anacrusis is ___.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: Why do pickups matter when counting a piece?
options: Because they add an extra beat to every bar.
Because the first bar is shorter, so the strong beats fall differently than you would expect.
Because they are always played slowly.
Because they change the key signature.
questions.correct_answer: Because the first bar is shorter, so the strong beats fall differently than you would expect.
questions.explanation: Counting that ignores a pickup puts every accent in the wrong place.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: In 3/4 time a melody starts on beat three. How many beats are missing from that first bar?
questions.explanation: The bar has three beats and only the third is played, so two are missing.
